the question of whether it is possible to fi nd a way to report lease contracts on the part of the lessor, which would be symmetrical with the way of reporting on the part of lessee.
the issue of the accounting for leases in the lessor’s fi nancial statements, especially the issue of lease revenue reporting, and its impact on the fi nancial statements.
the question whether the current method of reporting operating leases on the part of lessor is suitable and if not, what are the alternatives.

the current model of reporting operating leases is not suitable for the recording of the lessee, and it would be better to change it.
it is not possible, without gross distortion of financial position of lessor, to apply only one method of recording lease contracts on the part of lessor, as it is the case of the lessee.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current method of accounting for operating leases on the side of the lessor is not appropriate and should be revised.
the current approach to recording operating lease does not correspond to the nature of the lease relationship.

there is no single approach that could meet all the conditions for recording leases in the fi nancial statements of the lessor, and that it is necessary to use several approaches in order to achieve the desired results.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is no one approach that would meet the requirements of all lease contracts, but the existing model of reporting an operating lease is not consistent with the requirements of the International Accounting Standards and is also inconsistent with the requirements of IASB and FASB projects.

there is no one approach that is suitable for the recording of the lease relationship on the side of the lessor, which would be symmetrical and consistent with the approach used for recording of the same relationship on the side lessee.

the lessee’s approach to the recording of lease agreements on the side of the lessor, which is currently used in practice, is not the only way to record the lease agreement, but it is also possible to use the approach of performance obligations or derecognition.
